usage.description: Descriptive GIS and political-status context only. These fields are not used as adaptation-gap score inputs.

sources.name: United Nations Statistics Division M49 standard country or area codes and geographic regions
sources.caveats: Used for Pacific subregion labels and UN short-form country or area names, not political status. UNSD states that groupings are for statistical convenience and do not imply political affiliation or legal status.

sources.name: United Nations - Member States
sources.caveats: Used to support the high-level sovereign-state labels for Fiji, Kiribati, Nauru, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu, and as supporting context for the three freely associated sovereign countries.

sources.name: United Nations and Decolonization - Non-Self-Governing Territories
sources.caveats: Used to retain the separate UN Non-Self-Governing Territory context for American Samoa, French Polynesia, Guam, New Caledonia, Pitcairn, and Tokelau. Domestic administrative labels do not replace this UN context.

sources.name: U.S. Department of the Interior Office of Insular Affairs - American Samoa
sources.caveats: Used for the high-level U.S. territory label. The row does not attempt a full account of American Samoa's constitutional, self-determination, citizenship, or nationality context.

sources.name: U.S. Department of the Interior Office of Insular Affairs - Guam
sources.caveats: Supporting administering-government context; 48 U.S.C. 1421a supplies the more precise unincorporated-territory wording.

sources.name: U.S. Department of the Interior Office of Insular Affairs - Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands
sources.caveats: Supporting administering-government context; the Covenant in 48 U.S.C. 1801 supplies the precise public label.

sources.name: U.S. Department of the Interior Office of Insular Affairs - Federated States of Micronesia
sources.caveats: Supporting high-level Compact of Free Association context; 8 FAM 1306.1 supplies the reviewed sovereign-country wording.

sources.name: U.S. Department of the Interior Office of Insular Affairs - The Marshall Islands
sources.caveats: Supporting high-level Compact of Free Association context; 8 FAM 1306.1 supplies the reviewed sovereign-country wording.

sources.name: U.S. Department of the Interior Office of Insular Affairs - Republic of Palau
sources.caveats: Supporting high-level Compact of Free Association context; 8 FAM 1306.1 supplies the reviewed sovereign-country wording.

sources.name: U.S. House Office of the Law Revision Counsel - 48 U.S.C. 1421a
sources.caveats: Statutory source for Guam's unincorporated-territory label; the public line remains a short descriptive summary rather than a constitutional-law account.

sources.name: U.S. House Office of the Law Revision Counsel - 48 U.S.C. 1801 and Covenant
sources.caveats: Statutory source for the self-governing commonwealth, political-union, and U.S.-sovereignty wording.

sources.name: U.S. Department of State Foreign Affairs Manual - 8 FAM 1306.1
sources.caveats: Used for the reviewed description of the Federated States of Micronesia, Marshall Islands, and Palau as sovereign countries in free association with the United States. Compact provisions are summarized at a high level only.

sources.name: New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade - Cook Islands
sources.caveats: Used for self-government in free association with New Zealand. The public line does not summarize every constitutional, citizenship, or international-personality detail.

sources.name: New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade - Niue
sources.caveats: Used for self-government in free association with New Zealand. The public line does not summarize every constitutional, citizenship, or international-personality detail.

sources.name: New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade - Tokelau
sources.caveats: Used for the current non-self-governing territory within the Realm of New Zealand wording. The UN source independently records Tokelau's Non-Self-Governing Territory status.

sources.name: Legifrance - Constitution of 4 October 1958
sources.caveats: Used for French constitutional context, including article 74 collectivities, and as supporting context for Wallis and Futuna.

sources.name: Legifrance - Organic Law 2004-192 on the autonomy status of French Polynesia, article 1
sources.caveats: Used for French Polynesia's overseas-collectivity and overseas-country-within-the-Republic wording. The UN Non-Self-Governing Territory context is recorded separately.

sources.name: French Ministry for Overseas Territories - Wallis and Futuna
sources.caveats: Used with article 74 of the French Constitution for the high-level overseas-collectivity label. The row does not summarize Wallis and Futuna's customary institutions or full 1961 statutory framework.

sources.name: United Nations Secretariat - Working paper on New Caledonia, A/AC.109/2026/11
sources.caveats: Used for the current sui generis collectivity within the French Republic wording. The paper also records the proposed institutional transition; the public label does not present that proposal as implemented.

sources.name: French Senate - Constitutional bill concerning New Caledonia
sources.caveats: Used to confirm that the proposed constitutional change remained unfinished at review time. Recheck before any later publication because this status is dynamic and politically sensitive.

sources.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office - Pitcairn Island travel advice
sources.caveats: Used for the British Overseas Territory label. The UN Non-Self-Governing Territory context is recorded separately.

political_status_review.decision_rule: Use short current public wording supported by authoritative UN, administering-government, associated-state, statutory, or foreign-affairs sources; keep domestic administrative and UN decolonization contexts distinct; do not expose workflow flags or treat proposed legal changes as implemented.

artifact_caveats: All rows are descriptive GIS context and remain outside adaptation-gap scoring.
Pacific subregion labels follow UN M49 statistical groupings and are not cultural or political boundaries.
Short public political-status labels do not exhaust constitutional, self-determination, citizenship, nationality, treaty, or decolonization context.
New Caledonia's status is dynamic and politically sensitive; the reviewed line states current legal status and does not treat the proposed transition as implemented.
The table does not provide polygon boundaries or settle boundary-source choices.
review_recommendations: Recheck New Caledonia immediately before later publication because the constitutional process was unfinished on 2026-07-30.
Keep UN Non-Self-Governing Territory context distinct from domestic administrative wording for American Samoa, French Polynesia, Guam, New Caledonia, Pitcairn, and Tokelau.
Use this table for grouping and explanatory context only; do not join it into score calculations.
